<div class="mntl-sc-block-universal-callout__body"><ul><li>In a new PEOPLE cover story, Whitney Leavitt exclusively reveals that she will return to Broadway this winter in <em>Just in Time</em>, starring as Sandra Dee</li><li><em>The</em> <em>Secret Lives of Mormon Wives</em> star, 33, is making her Broadway comeback after breaking box office records in <em>Chicago</em> this spring</li><li>“I don’t know what’s going to be going on in my life. But I’ll for sure at least be there for six weeks,” she says of her planned run in the musical</li></ul></div>
</div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_2-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> <a href="https://people.com/whitney-leavitt-11859284" data-component="link" data-source="inlineLink" data-type="internalLink" data-ordinal="1">Whitney Leavitt</a> is headed back to Broadway.
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_3-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_4-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> In this week’s PEOPLE cover story, <a href="https://people.com/the-secret-lives-of-mormon-wives-will-return-for-season-6-12035794" data-component="link" data-source="inlineLink" data-type="internalLink" data-ordinal="1"><em>The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives</em></a> star, 33, reveals that she will return to the stage this winter to star in <a href="https://www.telecharge.com/Just-in-Time-tickets" data-component="link" data-source="inlineLink" data-type="externalLink" data-ordinal="2" rel="nocaes noopener" target="_blank"><em>Just in Time</em></a>, following a three-month run in <a href="https://people.com/whitney-leavitt-razzle-dazzles-in-debut-broadway-chicago-performance-11895910" data-component="link" data-source="inlineLink" data-type="internalLink" data-ordinal="3"><em>Chicago</em></a> that <a href="https://people.com/whitney-leavitt-chicago-run-breaks-box-office-record-11928132" data-component="link" data-source="inlineLink" data-type="internalLink" data-ordinal="4">broke the production’s box office record</a>.
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_5-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_6-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> “I’m so excited,” says Leavitt, who will play <a href="https://people.com/jonathan-groff-erika-henningsen-just-in-time-bobby-darin-sandra-dee-exclusive-11683218" data-component="link" data-source="inlineLink" data-type="internalLink" data-ordinal="1">teen idol Sandra Dee</a> in the hit musical, which traces the <a href="https://people.com/bobby-darin-the-brief-life-of-the-tragic-teen-idol-11727106" data-component="link" data-source="inlineLink" data-type="internalLink" data-ordinal="2">unbelievable true story of singer Bobby Darin</a> before his untimely death from a heart attack when he was just 37.
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_7-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"><div id="mm-ads-native-fluid_1-0" class="comp mm-ads-native-fluid mm-ads-native " style="--native-ad-height: auto" data-right-rail-index="2"><div id="mm-ads-native__adunit_1-0" class="comp mm-ads-native__adunit mm-ads-gpt-dynamic-adunit mm-ads-gpt-adunit scads-to-load gpt native js-immediate-ad js-immediate-ad-loaded">
<div id="native" class="wrapper" data-type="native" data-pos="native" data-priority="4" data-sizes="[[1, 3],"fluid",[600, 250]]" data-rtb="true" data-wait-for-third-party="false" data-targeting="{}"></div>
</div></div></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_8-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> Tony Award nominee <a href="https://people.com/jeremy-jordan-makes-a-splish-splash-as-bobby-darin-in-broadways-just-in-time-exclusive-photos-11957130" data-component="link" data-source="inlineLink" data-type="internalLink" data-ordinal="1">Jeremy Jordan</a> is currently leading <em>Just in Time</em> as Darin. Leavitt will star opposite him at New York City’s Circle in the Square Theatre for a limited six-week engagement beginning Tuesday, Dec. 1 through Sunday, Jan. 10, 2027.
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_9-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<figure id="mntl-sc-block_10-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block people-sc-block-image mntl-sc-block-image mntl-sc-block-image--no-theme no-theme figure-landscape figure-high-res"> <div class="figure-media">
<div class="img-placeholder" style="padding-bottom:66.6%;">
<img data-src="https://people.com/thmb/EN72BiJRue6eq_M1VLH-lC8noFE=/4000x0/filters:no_upscale():max_bytes(150000):strip_icc():focal(749x0:751x2):format(webp)/jonathan-gross-whitney-leavitt-081226-166400f078c24ceaa002bbe0934112a4.jpg" width="1500" height="1000" data-srcset="https://people.com/thmb/EN72BiJRue6eq_M1VLH-lC8noFE=/4000x0/filters:no_upscale():max_bytes(150000):strip_icc():focal(749x0:751x2):format(webp)/jonathan-gross-whitney-leavitt-081226-166400f078c24ceaa002bbe0934112a4.jpg 4000w" data-sizes="4000px" alt="Jonathan Groff; Whitney Leavitt " class=" mntl-image mntl-image universal-image__image lazyloadwait" data-expand="300" id="mntl-sc-block-image_1-0" data-click-tracked="true" data-img-lightbox-variant="" data-tracking-container="true" data-img-lightbox="true">

<span class="figure-article-caption-owner"><p>ANGELA WEISS/AFP via Getty; Dia Dipasupil/WireImage</p></span>
</figcaption></figure>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_11-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> Leavitt, who is <a href="https://people.com/why-is-whitney-leavitt-leaving-the-secret-lives-of-mormon-wives-11965080" data-component="link" data-source="inlineLink" data-type="internalLink" data-ordinal="1">leaving</a> <em>The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives</em> after season 5, says her journey back to Broadway began with a visit from <a href="https://people.com/jonathan-groff-8742167" data-component="link" data-source="inlineLink" data-type="internalLink" data-ordinal="2">Jonathan Groff</a>, who originated the lead role of Darin in the musical when it premiered in April 2025. 
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_12-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_13-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> “He’s the best of all time,” Leavitt says of Groff, 41. “One night, the <em>Chicago</em> stage manager tells me, ‘Oh, Jonathan Groff is here’... that immediately put a huge stressor on me, but it also motivated me. I wasn’t able to see him after the show, so I was like, ‘Okay, let me go see you in <em>Just in Time</em>.’ Phenomenal. Love watching that man perform.”
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_14-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_15-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> Her full-circle moment came only a few months later. “I got an audition for the role [of Sandra Dee],” she says. “We did it, we studied hard, and here we are. And I cannot wait to be a part of that show.”
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_16-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>

<p id="mntl-sc-block_18-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> Leavitt’s time starring as Roxie Hart in <em>Chicago</em>, originally also planned as a six-week run beginning in February 2026, ultimately <a href="https://people.com/whitney-leavitt-extends-her-run-in-broadway-chicago-11908684" data-component="link" data-source="inlineLink" data-type="internalLink" data-ordinal="1">extended</a> to three months. During her run, the production achieved its highest weekly box office gross in its 29-year history — a milestone she says is “definitely validating,” though she’s quick to emphasize that it was a team effort. 
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_19-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_20-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> “I’m going to tell you right now, that cast and crew, it was a group effort to be able to do that because we all pushed really hard to market it,” she says. “How can we find creative ways to get people to come and see the show? I’m so happy I got to be a part of that.”
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_21-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_22-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> As for how long she’ll be playing Dee, Darin’s former wife — who Leavitt affectionally describes as “a movie star” who “loves pink” — she says she’s “going to see how it goes.”
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_23-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_24-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> “A lot of times you have a runtime, and then you get to decide, ‘Do you want to stay or do you want to go?’ I think it’s too hard to tell right now. I don’t know what’s going to be going on in my life. But I’ll for sure at least be there for six weeks.”
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_25-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>

<p id="mntl-sc-block_28-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> Now, Leavitt is preparing to navigate the logistics of a bicoastal life. She and her husband, <a href="https://people.com/mormon-wives-conner-leavitt-joins-cast-of-11-to-midnight-exclusive-11963470" data-component="link" data-source="inlineLink" data-type="internalLink" data-ordinal="1">Conner Leavitt</a>, recently put down roots near their families in Utah with their <a href="https://people.com/all-about-whitney-leavitt-kids-11825321" data-component="link" data-source="inlineLink" data-type="internalLink" data-ordinal="2">three children</a> — Sedona, 6, Liam, 4, and Billy, 1 — but she’s excited for what’s ahead.
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_29-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_30-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> “I do get bored easily, unfortunately, but it also motivates me,” she says. “I just think it’s always been a part of me. I don’t really have plans on stopping, and I just want to keep going… I don’t plan on leaving the Broadway world anytime soon.”
</p>

<p id="mntl-sc-block_34-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> <em>Just in Time </em>is one of Broadway’s most recent hits. Developed and directed by Tony Award winner Alex Timbers, the musical began performances in March 2025, and opened to critical acclaim the following month. It’s the only musical of the 2024-2025 season to have recouped its capitalization.
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_35-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_36-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> Featuring a book by Tony winner Warren Leight (<em>Side Man</em>) and Isaac Oliver (<em>Intimacy Idiot</em>, <em>The Marvelous Mrs. Maisel</em>)<em>, Just in Time</em> is set to a score of Darin’s catalog of classics, including “Beyond the Sea,” “Mack the Knife,” “Splish Splash” and “Dream Lover.” The immersive musical transforms the theater into a swinging nightclub, where Jordan plays a version of himself telling the story of Darin’s meteoric rise from teen idol to global sensation.
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_37-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_38-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> In addition to Jordan, <em>Just in Time</em> currently stars Carrie St. Louis as Dee, as well as Olivia Holt, Debbie Gravitte, Joe Barbara, Emily Bergl, Lance Roberts, Caesar Samayoa, Christine Cornish, Julia Grondin, Valeria Yamin, Jaime Foord, Tari Kelly, Matt Magnusson, Jeffrey Schecter and Tristen Buettel.
</p>

</p>

gold_text: ‘The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives’ star shares in this week’s PEOPLE cover story that she will star as Sandra Dee in musical about the life of Dee’s former “Dream Lover,” Bobby Darin. Whitney Leavitt is headed back to Broadway. In this week’s PEOPLE cover story, The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives star, 33, reveals that she will return to the stage this winter to star in Just in Time, following a three-month run in Chicago that broke the production’s box office record. “I’m so excited,” says Leavitt, who will play teen idol Sandra Dee in the hit musical, which traces the unbelievable true story of singer Bobby Darin before his untimely death from a heart attack when he was just 37. Tony Award nominee Jeremy Jordan is currently leading Just in Time as Darin. Leavitt will star opposite him at New York City’s Circle in the Square Theatre for a limited six-week engagement beginning Tuesday, Dec. 1 through Sunday, Jan. 10, 2027. Leavitt, who is leaving The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives after season 5, says her journey back to Broadway began with a visit from Jonathan Groff, who originated the lead role of Darin in the musical when it premiered in April 2025.  “He’s the best of all time,” Leavitt says of Groff, 41. “One night, the Chicago stage manager tells me, ‘Oh, Jonathan Groff is here’... that immediately put a huge stressor on me, but it also motivated me. I wasn’t able to see him after the show, so I was like, ‘Okay, let me go see you in Just in Time.’ Phenomenal. Love watching that man perform.” Her full-circle moment came only a few months later. “I got an audition for the role [of Sandra Dee],” she says. “We did it, we studied hard, and here we are. And I cannot wait to be a part of that show.” Leavitt’s time starring as Roxie Hart in Chicago, originally also planned as a six-week run beginning in February 2026, ultimately extended to three months. During her run, the production achieved its highest weekly box office gross in its 29-year history — a milestone she says is “definitely validating,” though she’s quick to emphasize that it was a team effort. “I’m going to tell you right now, that cast and crew, it was a group effort to be able to do that because we all pushed really hard to market it,” she says. “How can we find creative ways to get people to come and see the show? I’m so happy I got to be a part of that.” As for how long she’ll be playing Dee, Darin’s former wife — who Leavitt affectionally describes as “a movie star” who “loves pink” — she says she’s “going to see how it goes.” “A lot of times you have a runtime, and then you get to decide, ‘Do you want to stay or do you want to go?’ I think it’s too hard to tell right now. I don’t know what’s going to be going on in my life. But I’ll for sure at least be there for six weeks.” Now, Leavitt is preparing to navigate the logistics of a bicoastal life. She and her husband, Conner Leavitt, recently put down roots near their families in Utah with their three children — Sedona, 6, Liam, 4, and Billy, 1 — but she’s excited for what’s ahead. “I do get bored easily, unfortunately, but it also motivates me,” she says. “I just think it’s always been a part of me. I don’t really have plans on stopping, and I just want to keep going… I don’t plan on leaving the Broadway world anytime soon.” Just in Time is one of Broadway’s most recent hits. Developed and directed by Tony Award winner Alex Timbers, the musical began performances in March 2025, and opened to critical acclaim the following month. It’s the only musical of the 2024-2025 season to have recouped its capitalization. Featuring a book by Tony winner Warren Leight (Side Man) and Isaac Oliver (Intimacy Idiot, The Marvelous Mrs. Maisel), Just in Time is set to a score of Darin’s catalog of classics, including “Beyond the Sea,” “Mack the Knife,” “Splish Splash” and “Dream Lover.” The immersive musical transforms the theater into a swinging nightclub, where Jordan plays a version of himself telling the story of Darin’s meteoric rise from teen idol to global sensation. In addition to Jordan, Just in Time currently stars Carrie St. Louis as Dee, as well as Olivia Holt, Debbie Gravitte, Joe Barbara, Emily Bergl, Lance Roberts, Caesar Samayoa, Christine Cornish, Julia Grondin, Valeria Yamin, Jaime Foord, Tari Kelly, Matt Magnusson, Jeffrey Schecter and Tristen Buettel. Tickets for Just in Time are on sale now. For more on Whitney Leavitt, pick up this week’s issue of PEOPLE, on newsstands Friday.

<div class="mntl-sc-block-universal-callout__body"><ul><li>Kelsie Watts, a cast member in <em>Moulin Rouge! The Musical </em>on Broadway, shared a surprising story via Instagram</li><li>The actress detailed a fight that “almost broke out” between audience members sitting in the front two rows of a recent performance</li><li>Addressing theater etiquette, she said, “Should we ever go to another theater show, maybe, maybe, we just are respectful to the rest of the audience members around us”</li></ul></div>
</div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_2-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> <a class="null" href="https://people.com/moulin-rouge-cast-and-crew-crazy-about-megan-thee-stallion-exclusive-11944867" data-type="" data-component="link" data-source="inlineLink" data-ordinal="1" rel="noopener noreferrer"><em>Moulin Rouge! The Musical</em></a><em> </em>is going out with a bang on Broadway. Equally explosive, apparently, are its audience members.
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_3-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_4-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> Kelsie Watts, who currently stars as Satine in the <a class="null" href="https://people.com/tag/tony-awards/" data-type="" data-component="link" data-source="inlineLink" data-ordinal="1" rel="noopener noreferrer">Tony Award</a>-winning musical, said in <a class="null" href="https://www.instagram.com/reels/Db6Jv28RPPK/" data-component="link" data-source="inlineLink" data-type="externalLink" data-ordinal="2" rel="null noopener" target="_blank">an Instagram video</a> on Tuesday, Aug. 11, that during a recent performance, “a fight almost broke out” between front-seat viewers.
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_5-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_6-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> “I’m here to tell you the story,” she began, addressing the camera.
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_7-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_8-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> “Apparently the front row and the second row had beefed the entire show,” Watts recalled of the night in question, shouting out the ushers and security team at the Al Hirschfeld Theatre, where <em>Moulin Rouge! The Musical</em> is playing until its closing performance on Aug. 30.
</p>

<p id="mntl-sc-block_11-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> “I guess the people in the second row were talking too loud; they were kicking chairs,” the actress said. “And keep in mind, these people are in their 50s. We’re not talking about little kids.”
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_12-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_13-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> At a point in the show when Watts approaches the audience up close, when “you can see up my nostrils,” she quipped, “They are still, ‘Talk, talk, talk, talk, talk.’ We can hear everything, y’all. And not only is it distracting to us — it’s our job to work past it, so I get that — but you have so many people around you that have paid really good money to also experience this show.”
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_14-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_15-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> A woman in the front row “stands up, turns around and starts yelling over her seat,” Watts recalled. “All of this is happening while I have this ginormous hat on my head. I’m in this little muff and this dress that I’m just trying to make sure I don’t lose my balance in.”
</p>

</p>

gold_text: The Broadway adaptation of the 2001 movie will play its final performance on the Great White Way on Aug. 30. Moulin Rouge! The Musical is going out with a bang on Broadway. Equally explosive, apparently, are its audience members. Kelsie Watts, who currently stars as Satine in the Tony Award-winning musical, said in an Instagram video on Tuesday, Aug. 11, that during a recent performance, “a fight almost broke out” between front-seat viewers. “I’m here to tell you the story,” she began, addressing the camera. “Apparently the front row and the second row had beefed the entire show,” Watts recalled of the night in question, shouting out the ushers and security team at the Al Hirschfeld Theatre, where Moulin Rouge! The Musical is playing until its closing performance on Aug. 30. “I guess the people in the second row were talking too loud; they were kicking chairs,” the actress said. “And keep in mind, these people are in their 50s. We’re not talking about little kids.” At a point in the show when Watts approaches the audience up close, when “you can see up my nostrils,” she quipped, “They are still, ‘Talk, talk, talk, talk, talk.’ We can hear everything, y’all. And not only is it distracting to us — it’s our job to work past it, so I get that — but you have so many people around you that have paid really good money to also experience this show.” A woman in the front row “stands up, turns around and starts yelling over her seat,” Watts recalled. “All of this is happening while I have this ginormous hat on my head. I’m in this little muff and this dress that I’m just trying to make sure I don’t lose my balance in.” After making eye contact with a nearby usher, Watts recalled moving on with the show like normal. “But let me tell you, it took everything in me to not stop that show and be like, ‘What are y’all doing?’ ” she said. “I guess eventually the lady in the second row was put into a timeout in the lobby,” Watts added. “So I think this is a good learning experience that, should we ever go to another theater show, maybe, maybe, we just are respectful to the rest of the audience members around us.” She concluded, “I would have been just as frustrated if I had paid hundreds of dollars to sit in the front row of a closing show that I was in love with, to then just be bothered by people behind me kicking my seat and yelling just to be difficult. PEOPLE has reached out to a rep for Moulin Rouge! The Musical. Watts, a Texas native who competed on Season 19 of NBC’s The Voice, made her Broadway debut in February 2025 as Jane Seymour in the musical Six. She stars alongside Christian Douglas, Eric Anderson, André Ward and more in Moulin Rouge! The Musical. Tony winner Aaron Tveit, who originated the lead role of Christian, returns to the show for 15 performances later this month. The musical is based on the 2001 movie starring Nicole Kidman and Ewan McGregor. It won 10 Tony Awards in 2021, including Best Musical. Directed by Alex Timbers with a book by John Logan, the production features a score that incorporates over 70 pop hits from the 1940s to the 2010s, plus “Come What May,” the ballad from the film. Tickets for Moulin Rouge! The Musical are on sale now.

<div id="article-content_1-0" class="comp article-content mntl-block"><div id="mntl-sc-page_1-0" class="comp mntl-sc-page mntl-block structured-content" data-sc-sticky-offset="90" data-sc-ad-label-height="24" data-sc-ad-track-spacing="100" data-sc-min-track-height="250" data-sc-max-track-height="600" data-sc-breakpoint="50em" data-sc-load-immediate="4" data-sc-content-positions="[1, 1250, 1550, 1950, 2350, 2750, 3150, 3550, 3950]" data-bind-scroll-on-start="true"><div id="mntl-sc-block_1-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block people-sc-block-callout mntl-sc-block-universal-callout theme-needtoknow" data-tracking-id="mntl-sc-block-callout" data-tracking-container="true"> <h3 class="mntl-sc-block-universal-callout__heading">NEED TO KNOW</h3>
<div class="mntl-sc-block-universal-callout__body"><ul><li>Investigators discovered human remains at Arizona’s Patagonia State Park in April 1978</li><li>While the condition of the remains left investigators with no way to identify the man, they determined that the victim, likely a young adult male between the ages of 18 and 24, died by drowning</li><li>Nearly 50 years later, investigators used DNA technology to confirm that the remains belonged to David Alan McInroy</li></ul></div>
</div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_2-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> Human remains discovered nearly 50 years ago at an Arizona state park have since been identified as a missing Canadian man.
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_3-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_4-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> Earlier this month, the Santa Cruz Sheriff’s Office announced that the remains that were found on April 28, 1978, at Patagonia Lake State Park in Santa Cruz County have been identified as belonging to David Alan McInroy, according to <a class="null" href="https://www.cp24.com/news/canada/2026/08/11/man-who-drowned-in-arizona-almost-50-years-ago-was-from-ontario-local-police/" data-type="" data-component="link" data-source="inlineLink" data-ordinal="1" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">CP24</a>, CBS affiliate <a class="null" href="https://www.kold.com/2026/08/06/dna-technology-helps-solve-decades-old-cold-case-santa-cruz-county/" data-type="" data-component="link" data-source="inlineLink" data-ordinal="2" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">KOLD</a> and <a class="null" href="https://www.winnipegsun.com/national-news/ontario-mans-1978-death-in-arizona-finally-solved/article_c2903762-716f-449a-aef4-ce02aeaa3489.html" data-type="" data-component="link" data-source="inlineLink" data-ordinal="3" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"><em>The Winnipeg Sun</em></a>. 
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_5-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_6-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> Investigators discovered the remains alongside a few articles of clothing — including denim cut-off shorts with a “Made in Canada” tag, white Jockey-brand shorts, dark-colored socks and ankle-high walking boots, according to DNA laboratory <a class="null" href="https://dnasolves.com/articles/santa-cruz-county-arizona-1978-david-alan-mcinroy/" data-type="" data-component="link" data-source="inlineLink" data-ordinal="1" rel="noopener noreferrer nofollow" target="_blank">Othram</a>.
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_7-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_8-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block people-sc-block-featuredlink--people-app-promo mntl-block"><a href="https://people-app.onelink.me/HNIa/kz7l4cuf" target="_blank" rel="noopener nofollow nocaes" class="iosLink mntl-text-link " id="iosLink_1-0" data-tracking-container="true"><div id="people-app-promo__left_1-0" class="comp people-app-promo__left mntl-block"><svg class="icon people-app-promo__logo ">

<p id="mntl-sc-block_10-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> While the condition of the remains left investigators with no way to identify the man, they determined that he died by drowning and was likely a young man between the ages of 18 and 24, Othram said.
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_11-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_12-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> “The individual also had no identification on them whatsoever,” Undersheriff Gerardo Castillo told CP24 of the man, who became known as “Santa Cruz County John Doe (1978).”
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_13-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_14-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> As DNA technology continued to improve over the years, Othram reported that the Santa Cruz County Sheriff’s Office worked with the Pima County Medical Examiner’s Office to submit forensic evidence to the Texas-based genetic genealogy firm in August 2024.
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_15-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>

<p id="mntl-sc-block_18-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> Othram then developed a DNA extract and used Forensic-Grade Genome Sequencing to build a comprehensive DNA profile for the man, which was used to develop new investigative leads that were returned to law enforcement.
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_19-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_20-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> Eventually, the investigation led to the positive identification of McInroy, who was born in Ontario on Oct. 13, 1952. He was 26 at the time of his death. 
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_21-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_22-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block people-sc-block-callout mntl-sc-block-universal-callout theme-generic" data-tracking-id="mntl-sc-block-callout" data-tracking-container="true">

<p id="mntl-sc-block_23-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> Noting that McInroy’s loved ones had not been in touch with him since before he found himself in Arizona, Castillo emphasized to CP24 how important it was to finally “give closure” to his family.
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_24-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>

gold_text: Undersheriff Gerardo Castillo said how important it was to finally give closure to David Alan McInroy’s family. Human remains discovered nearly 50 years ago at an Arizona state park have since been identified as a missing Canadian man. Earlier this month, the Santa Cruz Sheriff’s Office announced that the remains that were found on April 28, 1978, at Patagonia Lake State Park in Santa Cruz County have been identified as belonging to David Alan McInroy, according to CP24, CBS affiliate KOLD and The Winnipeg Sun. Investigators discovered the remains alongside a few articles of clothing — including denim cut-off shorts with a “Made in Canada tag, white Jockey-brand shorts, dark-colored socks and ankle-high walking boots, according to DNA laboratory Othram. While the condition of the remains left investigators with no way to identify the man, they determined that he died by drowning and was likely a young man between the ages of 18 and 24, Othram said. “The individual also had no identification on them whatsoever, Undersheriff Gerardo Castillo told CP24 of the man, who became known as “Santa Cruz County John Doe (1978). As DNA technology continued to improve over the years, Othram reported that the Santa Cruz County Sheriff’s Office worked with the Pima County Medical Examiner’s Office to submit forensic evidence to the Texas-based genetic genealogy firm in August 2024. Othram then developed a DNA extract and used Forensic-Grade Genome Sequencing to build a comprehensive DNA profile for the man, which was used to develop new investigative leads that were returned to law enforcement. Eventually, the investigation led to the positive identification of McInroy, who was born in Ontario on Oct. 13, 1952. He was 26 at the time of his death. Noting that McInroy’s loved ones had not been in touch with him since before he found himself in Arizona, Castillo emphasized to CP24 how important it was to finally “give closure to his family. The Santa Cruz Sheriff’s Office did not immediately respond to PEOPLE’s request for comment.

<div id="article-content_1-0" class="comp article-content mntl-block"><div id="mntl-sc-page_1-0" class="comp mntl-sc-page mntl-block structured-content" data-sc-sticky-offset="90" data-sc-ad-label-height="24" data-sc-ad-track-spacing="100" data-sc-min-track-height="250" data-sc-max-track-height="600" data-sc-breakpoint="50em" data-sc-load-immediate="4" data-sc-content-positions="[1, 1250, 1550, 1950, 2350, 2750, 3150, 3550, 3950]" data-bind-scroll-on-start="true"><div id="mntl-sc-block_1-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block people-sc-block-callout mntl-sc-block-universal-callout theme-needtoknow" data-tracking-id="mntl-sc-block-callout" data-tracking-container="true"> <h3 class="mntl-sc-block-universal-callout__heading">NEED TO KNOW</h3>
<div class="mntl-sc-block-universal-callout__body"><ul><li>Hoku opens up to PEOPLE about why she walked away from her pop career in the early 2000s</li><li>The musician, who recently made a rare public appearance at the “Elle World” event in New York City, also reveals she’s been working on new music in the pop space</li><li>Hoku’s last release was her single “Greater” in 2020</li></ul></div>
</div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_2-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> Amid the sea of blonde pop stars in the early aughts like <a class="null" href="https://people.com/tag/britney-spears/" data-component="link" data-source="inlineLink" data-type="internalLink" data-ordinal="1" rel="null">Britney Spears</a>, <a class="null" href="https://people.com/tag/christina-aguilera/" data-component="link" data-source="inlineLink" data-type="internalLink" data-ordinal="2" rel="null">Christina Aguilera</a>, <a class="null" href="https://people.com/tag/mandy-moore/" data-component="link" data-source="inlineLink" data-type="internalLink" data-ordinal="3" rel="null">Mandy Moore</a> and <a class="null" href="https://people.com/tag/jessica-simpson/" data-component="link" data-source="inlineLink" data-type="internalLink" data-ordinal="4" rel="null">Jessica Simpson</a> came <a class="null" href="https://www.instagram.com/heyitshoku/" data-component="link" data-source="inlineLink" data-type="externalLink" data-ordinal="5" rel="null noopener" target="_blank">Hoku</a>. If you were a millennial between 2000 and 2001, it would have been near-impossible to be unfamiliar with Hoku’s first single <a class="null" href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nG7T9q48ggQ" data-component="link" data-source="inlineLink" data-type="externalLink" data-ordinal="6" rel="null noopener" target="_blank">“Another Dumb Blonde”</a> or her second bubbly juggernaut <a class="null" href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zXYLMevMsd0" data-component="link" data-source="inlineLink" data-type="externalLink" data-ordinal="7" rel="null noopener" target="_blank">“Perfect Day,”</a> which became the infectious intro song to the 2001 hit comedy <a class="null" href="https://people.com/where-is-legally-blonde-cast-now-12009483" data-component="link" data-source="inlineLink" data-type="internalLink" data-ordinal="8" rel="null"><em>Legally Blonde</em></a>.
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_3-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_4-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> But not long after releasing her self-titled debut album, just as the Hawaiian-born singer was blossoming as a pop star, she walked away from the spotlight. “I did mourn that things were not different, and I mourned that around 21, 22, my dream was over... but now I just feel so much gratitude because I stepped out,” Hoku, now 45, says, adjusting the flower from her ear on a Zoom call from her home in Los Angeles.
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_5-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_6-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> Out of the public eye, Hoku (born Hoku Christian Ho) spent the last two decades raising her three kids — a 17-year-old daughter, a 15-year-old son and a 12-year-old son — living a quiet life and quietly writing music. For a moment in 2018, she returned with the Christian EP <em>Called by Name</em> and the single “Greater” in 2020. But she’s since stepped back from her faith as well. “It stopped feeling authentic,” she says.
</p>

<p id="mntl-sc-block_9-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> In June, for the first time in years, Hoku made a rare appearance and performance at “Elle World” ahead of the premiere of the prequel series <em>Elle</em>. And now, she’s eyeing a comeback.
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_10-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_11-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> Below, Hoku opens up to PEOPLE about why she left the music industry, leaving her faith behind and the surprising celebrity fans she’s made over the years.
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_12-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_13-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> <strong>PEOPLE: How did <em>Legally Blonde</em> and its use of </strong><a class="null" href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zXYLMevMsd0" data-component="link" data-source="inlineLink" data-type="externalLink" data-ordinal="1" rel="null noopener" target="_blank"><strong>“Perfect Day”</strong></a><strong> change your life?</strong>
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_14-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_15-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> <strong>HOKU: </strong>“Perfect Day” came at the end of what became the end of my music career, but it was this lovely little period where the song was really connecting with people. I was touring it, and then in the movie it was a bit of an afterthought for my label. There was a lot of like, “Well, this movie’s probably not going to be that.” It was kind of low-budget; it was a female-led movie. But it ended up being the most defining song of my career, and I feel so thankful for that. The movie itself is such a special movie and so in line with who I am as a person. It feels really good to have that be such a big part of my legacy.
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_16-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>

<p id="mntl-sc-block_18-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> <strong>PEOPLE: In the early aughts it felt like you were really gaining momentum and then you disappeared. What happened between you and your record label after the release of “Perfect Day”?</strong>
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_19-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_20-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> <strong>HOKU: </strong>“Perfect Day” was meant to be the lead single for my follow-up album, and it was associated with the movie. The movie did a lot more than people were expecting. So I was touring it, performing it live, but behind the scenes, there were conversations about my next album. And by then, my label and I ... specifically one person at the label; he was a creep. He was exactly one of those people that you hear about, and he was really in charge of everything with my music. There had been a lot of pressure from everyone — him included — to sexualize my image, be willing to put out the vibe that I was down for whatever to all these radio people.
</p>

<p id="mntl-sc-block_23-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> I loved the music. I loved the singing. I loved the performing. It had been my dream, but there was just this “hunted” feeling; this “I’m prey amongst predators” kind of feeling. That was just how the industry worked back then. So, I was already kind of thinking to myself, “I don’t know if this is worth it for me anymore.” Then, this guy made an ultimatum, and was like, “You will do X, Y, and Z. I’m sick of you teasing me enough, or I’m going to bury your record.” And I was like, “Okay.” I got up, walked out of that meeting and that was it. That was the end of that. 
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_24-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_25-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> The spin I put on it was that it wasn’t in line with my faith, which at the time was very true. I was a very devoted Christian at that time. I’ve since stepped out of my faith, but that was true to some degree. It wasn’t something I was comfortable with. I was 18, 19, 20, 21. I was just barely coming into my own sexuality at that point. [I] didn’t feel like marketing that to the masses, but ultimately it did come down to an ultimatum. So I walked away. 
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_26-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_27-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> <strong>PEOPLE: From what I understand, you were also married at the time, and the record label wanted you to pretend that you weren’t. Tell me about that.</strong>
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_28-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_29-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> <strong>HOKU: </strong>Yes. That was the big secret of my music career — that I was married the whole time! I’m still married to him. We still love each other very much. We just celebrated 27 years. I realized that’s not normal for young married people to be like that. But I do feel really lucky. At the time it felt so unjust. But in retrospect, I do understand a little bit of, “We’re not going to market that this teenybopper pop star is married.”
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_30-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_31-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> What bothered me was that there was this guy [at] the label [that] was like, “You need to get divorced. How long ago did you get married? Can we annul this?” That was one of the first meetings we had. Things just never really improved from there. I wouldn’t travel or tour without [my husband] because he very much felt like my protector during a time when I was feeling very hunted, like I was saying. They ended up being like, “Okay, well, we might as well give him a job.” So then he was working alongside my tour manager during my last summer that I was touring. He ended up getting into the business side of things, but in the beginning he was just my guy.
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_32-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_33-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> (PEOPLE has reached out to Universal Music, the parent company of Interscope/Geffen Records, for comment.)
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_34-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_35-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> <strong>PEOPLE: You ended up walking away from your pop career. At this juncture, do you have any regrets about that?</strong>
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_36-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_37-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> <strong>HOKU:</strong> Not at this juncture. I did then. Not that I would have stayed in the environment I was in, but I did mourn that things were not different, and I mourned that around 21, 22, my dream was over. This thing I’d worked for my whole life since I was 11 and singing on my dad’s show … there was a lot of mourning throughout in the interim time, but now I just feel so much gratitude because I stepped out.
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_38-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_39-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> I was able to raise my family in peace because I had gotten out of the game before anything got too out of hand. I left before the whole paparazzi tabloid culture was really a thing. I’m watching all these girls just getting out of limos at parties, trying to go grocery shopping, having these purposely unflattering photos taken of them and that whole critical attitude towards women’s bodies; I was able to sidestep that. I just got to go live my life in relative peace, so that was nice. I don’t regret it at all now.
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_40-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<figure id="mntl-sc-block_41-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block people-sc-block-image mntl-sc-block-image mntl-sc-block-image--no-theme no-theme figure-portrait figure-high-res"> <div class="figure-media">

<p id="mntl-sc-block_42-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> <strong>PEOPLE: In the early 2000s, the typical mainstream pop star was white and blonde for the most part. As a multiracial artist who is a part of the AAPI community, were there any pressures you felt at the time?</strong>
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_43-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_44-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> <strong>HOKU:</strong> I felt like I’m very white-passing. I’m blonde; I have pale skin. Everyone in my family is not. I’m the “white sheep” of my family. So, I’ve always had a little bit of a feeling already that I don’t belong in my culture. I don’t look associated with the culture I identify most with, which would be my local Hawaiian and Asian mixed culture that exists there. I grew up feeling very connected to that, but also having people yell at me in the water like, “Hey haole, get off my wave.” I’m like, “I’m one of you.” So there’s always been a little bit of sadness around not being able to be more visually connected to my culture.
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_45-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_46-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> There is always a little bit of imposter syndrome, this low-key sense of, “Gosh, look how pale I am. Look how blonde I am. Maybe I don’t have a right to represent my culture. Maybe I don’t have a right to be saying that I am Asian or Hawaiian.” But that was also very much a part of my marketing. It was a lot about [being] Hawaiian because my dad is very associated with Hawaii, and less about [being] Asian, even though my dad raised us very Asian. His dad was a Chinese chef. 
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_47-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_48-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> What I felt the most was: Is it okay that I want to represent this? Am I allowed? But also I was very proud of the fact that my Hawaiianness was on the forefront, and that I was able to represent home. Because the people of Hawaii were so excited that one of their own was there and making it in the industry. There’s probably, at that time, this weird, subconscious sense of imposter syndrome around claiming parts of my ethnicity that I didn’t visually represent in my mind. I think now [that] I looked more Asian than I thought at the time. As I look back at my life, I’m like — it was just the coloring and the kind of childhood weirdness that I hadn’t really processed yet.
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_49-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_50-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> <strong>PEOPLE: That’s really challenging. Thank you for sharing that.</strong>
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_51-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_52-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> <strong>HOKU: </strong>It’s weird. It’s been an interesting journey throughout my life. Because even after I walked away from my pop music, there was a hot minute where I was trying to do some acting. And I just remember one of the roles I lost out on was the role <a href="https://people.com/tag/hilary-duff/" data-component="link" data-source="inlineLink" data-type="internalLink" data-ordinal="1">Hilary Duff</a> got in <em>Cheaper by the Dozen</em>. I was far along, and once she got the part, I was like, “Well, duh, she looks like <a class="null" href="https://people.com/bonnie-hunt-remembers-robin-williams-jumanji-8746418" data-component="link" data-source="inlineLink" data-type="internalLink" data-ordinal="2" rel="null">Bonnie Hunt</a> and <a class="null" href="https://people.com/tag/steve-martin/" data-component="link" data-source="inlineLink" data-type="internalLink" data-ordinal="3" rel="null">Steve Martin</a>’s daughter. I don’t really.” I wasn’t getting called in for Asian roles or Hawaiian roles; I was getting called in for these [roles like] “You’re the cheerleader that gets killed. You’re the bimbo at the party.” And then I was just like, “Well, I don’t fit here either.”
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_53-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_54-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> I never felt like I really fit, and I feel like it’s actually been the interim time that I’ve really made peace with the fact that, <em>no, </em>I am these things. <em>This is my culture, these are my people, this is who I am. </em>I’ve made that journey over the years, but definitely had not at 18, 19, 20, 21.
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_55-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<figure id="mntl-sc-block_56-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block people-sc-block-image mntl-sc-block-image mntl-sc-block-image--no-theme no-theme figure-portrait figure-high-res"> <div class="figure-media">
<div class="img-placeholder" style="padding-bottom:125.0%;">

<p id="mntl-sc-block_57-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> <strong>PEOPLE: Your highest-charting single was “Another Dumb Blonde” and not “Perfect Day.” Does that remain surprising for you?</strong>
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_58-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_59-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> <strong>HOKU:</strong> It doesn’t [surprise me] because of where the industry was at the time. It was the end of the CD era and the beginning of the downloads era. [With] “Another Dumb Blonde,” I kept being told, “Oh yeah, it’s got this many CDs sold, but then it has this many downloads on Napster” or whatever. The idea was if it weren’t for these downloads, you would have had so much more. Certainly by the time “Perfect Day” had come out, there was a lot more of that. 
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_60-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_61-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block people-sc-block-embed mntl-sc-block-universal-embed mntl-sc-block-embed--youtube"><iframe id="mntl-sc-block_61-0-iframe" class="mntl-sc-block-universal-embed--iframe-legacy lazyloadwait" allowfullscreen="false" frameborder="0" sandbox="allow-forms allow-popups allow-popups-to-escape-sandbox allow-same-origin allow-scripts allow-top-navigation-by-user-activation" title="Hoku via YouTube" data-expand="300" data-src="/embed?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3DnG7T9q48ggQ&id=mntl-sc-block_61-0-iframe&options=e30%3D&docId=12037733"></iframe></div>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_62-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_63-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> <strong>PEOPLE: You have three kids now. What do they think of your career as a pop star? </strong>
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_64-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_65-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> <strong>HOKU: </strong>They’ve known about it since around elementary school [with] other people at their school, the moms, putting it together. So, it’s been a part of their lives in theory, but there wasn’t really an opportunity for them to really understand what it was like or really wrap their head around it.
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_66-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_67-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> But then when I got to do this “Elle World” event, I took them all with me, and they got to see me in my pop-star mode performing my songs. That was a really cool moment for me and for us to be able to share that. I think my kids all appreciate my pop stuff, but I wouldn’t say that they listen to it a ton. If I had to pick one, they all love <a class="null" href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qMoVIuCnhho" data-component="link" data-source="inlineLink" data-type="externalLink" data-ordinal="1" rel="null noopener" target="_blank">“How Do I Feel (The Burrito Song).”</a> I don’t know why. Since they got to watch me perform, I noticed them listening to it a lot more often, but they prefer the songs that I just play around the house that I’ve been writing during their lifetime.
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_68-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_69-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block people-sc-block-embed mntl-sc-block-universal-embed mntl-sc-block-embed--youtube"><iframe id="mntl-sc-block_69-0-iframe" class="mntl-sc-block-universal-embed--iframe-legacy lazyloadwait" allowfullscreen="false" frameborder="0" sandbox="allow-forms allow-popups allow-popups-to-escape-sandbox allow-same-origin allow-scripts allow-top-navigation-by-user-activation" title="Hoku via YouTube" data-expand="300" data-src="/embed?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3DqMoVIuCnhho&id=mntl-sc-block_69-0-iframe&options=e30%3D&docId=12037733"></iframe></div>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_70-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_71-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> <strong>PEOPLE: Between 2001 and 2018, were you focusing on raising your kids, or did you start another career?</strong>
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_72-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_73-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> <strong>HOKU:</strong> No, I just kind of focused on raising my kids. I had the luxury of being able to do that, and I really wanted to just devote myself to that, so I was lucky that I got to do that.
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_74-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_75-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block people-sc-block-callout mntl-sc-block-universal-callout theme-generic" data-tracking-id="mntl-sc-block-callout" data-tracking-container="true">

</div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_76-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> <strong>PEOPLE: In 2018, you released a Christian EP, as well as a single in 2020. What prompted you to step away from your faith, and when did that happen?</strong>
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_77-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_78-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> <strong>HOKU: </strong>That Christian album was the last gasp of me trying to make sense of what I believed. When I became a Christian, it was in Hawaii and in this sort of hippie way. It was like “Jesus is love, man.” I really just resonated with that message of inclusivity. In Hawaii, there is a lot of inclusivity racially [and in terms of] sexual orientation, and I was lucky in California to be in spaces that still fostered that sense of inclusivity. But as I saw the church, the “Big C” church devolve into this place that didn’t at all feel centered around what had connected me to it in the first place, I started to step back and question some of the things that I had been believing over time.
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_79-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_80-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> I think of my faith now as an expansion of what I used to believe. I believe in a higher power. I believe in the universe. I call it whatever I feel like in the moment. But I think that Christianity has become very much about labels [and] boxes. It stopped feeling authentic. I didn’t feel like I had to be so sure of everything. I’m okay with the gray area now. I still have so much love for people in my life that are still in that world, but I feel like I’ve evolved a little bit past that in my personal beliefs. It was definitely a journey, and at times very painful, because not everyone in my life was still my friend or still loving me once I made this decision. But ultimately I have to live authentically and be true to what I actually think and feel instead of trying to remain part of some club. 
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_81-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>

<p id="mntl-sc-block_84-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> <strong>PEOPLE: Back in the early 2000s, what was your favorite celebrity encounter you had?</strong>
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_85-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_86-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> <strong>HOKU: </strong>There are so many lovely people. <a class="null" href="https://people.com/rachael-leigh-cook-11800157" data-component="link" data-source="inlineLink" data-type="internalLink" data-ordinal="1" rel="null">Rachael Leigh Cook</a> and I would always run into each other at events, and every time we would see each other, we were like, “Oh, hi.” It was always nice to see her and catch up with her. I was obviously on the tour circuit that included a lot of the pop artists. So Mandy [Moore’s] manager and my manager were friends and then Jessica Simpson was dating <a class="null" href="https://people.com/tag/nick-lachey/" data-component="link" data-source="inlineLink" data-type="internalLink" data-ordinal="2" rel="null">Nick Lachey</a>, so then I did the <a class="null" href="https://people.com/tag/98-degrees/" data-component="link" data-source="inlineLink" data-type="internalLink" data-ordinal="3" rel="null">98 Degrees</a> special and we were in the same tour circuit.
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_87-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_88-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> We were all very friendly, but I think there’s a little more competition there, but not in any overt way. <a class="null" href="https://people.com/tag/jennifer-love-hewitt/" data-component="link" data-source="inlineLink" data-type="internalLink" data-ordinal="1" rel="null">Jennifer Love Hewitt</a> and I had a great encounter, [and] <a class="null" href="https://people.com/tag/kobe-bryant/" data-component="link" data-source="inlineLink" data-type="internalLink" data-ordinal="2" rel="null">Kobe Bryant</a>. He was just so gracious. <a class="null" href="https://people.com/tag/lance-bass/" data-component="link" data-source="inlineLink" data-type="internalLink" data-ordinal="3" rel="null">Lance Bass</a> [and] <a class="null" href="https://people.com/tag/chris-kirkpatrick/" data-component="link" data-source="inlineLink" data-type="internalLink" data-ordinal="4" rel="null">Chris Kirkpatrick</a> were very sweet. So, no ill will or bad blood. We were all just kind of out there doing our thing and happy to see each other.
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_89-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_90-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> <strong>PEOPLE: “Perfect Day” has had so much longevity, and especially on TikTok there’s been celebs and fans making videos. Earlier this year, for instance, </strong><a class="null" href="https://people.com/tag/hilary-duff/" data-component="link" data-source="inlineLink" data-type="internalLink" data-ordinal="1" rel="null"><strong>Hilary Duff</strong></a><strong> </strong><a class="null" href="https://www.tiktok.com/@hilaryduff/video/7600253741274516767" data-component="link" data-source="inlineLink" data-type="externalLink" data-ordinal="2" rel="null noopener" target="_blank"><strong>made one</strong></a><strong> when she was making her return to the stage, which is funny because I know a remix of “Perfect Day” was used in <em>Lizzie McGuire</em>. Is there a favorite fan or celeb TikTok video or edit that you have featuring the song?</strong>
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_91-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_92-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> <strong>HOKU: </strong>I mean, definitely Hilary. That was just so cute, and I appreciated that homage as she was making her reentry back into music. It got the most legs, for sure, that I’ve seen. 
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_93-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_94-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block people-sc-block-embed mntl-sc-block-universal-embed "><iframe id="mntl-sc-block_94-0-iframe" class="mntl-sc-block-universal-embed--iframe-legacy lazyloadwait" allowfullscreen="false" frameborder="0" sandbox="allow-forms allow-popups allow-popups-to-escape-sandbox allow-same-origin allow-scripts allow-top-navigation-by-user-activation" title="Hilary Duff via TikTok" data-expand="300" data-src="/embed?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.tiktok.com%2F%40hilaryduff%2Fvideo%2F7600253741274516767&id=mntl-sc-block_94-0-iframe&options=e30%3D&docId=12037733"></iframe></div>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_95-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_96-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> <strong>PEOPLE: Throughout the last two decades, is there a celebrity fan of “Perfect Day” that’s surprised you?</strong>
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_97-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_98-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> <strong>HOKU: </strong>At the “Elle World” event, I found out that <a class="null" href="https://people.com/bowen-yang-8742178" data-component="link" data-source="inlineLink" data-type="internalLink" data-ordinal="1" rel="null">Bowen Yang</a> and <a class="null" href="https://people.com/bowen-yang-matt-rogers-friendship-in-photos-12000001" data-component="link" data-source="inlineLink" data-type="internalLink" data-ordinal="2" rel="null">Matt Rogers</a> were going to be hosting the panel, and I was so excited. I love them, and I love Bowen. I watched <em>SNL</em> when he was on it, and I just think he’s so funny. He’s Asian, so I was just like, “Oh, it’s one of my people.” And in the limo ride over or the Escalade ride over, I turned back to my family [and] was like, “You guys, I think I might die if Bowen Yang knows who I am. That would be just the dream if he knew who I was.”
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_99-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_100-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> So, when I get there and we’re getting ready for the whole photo op, Bowen is right in front of me getting ready. [The person with me] was like, “Do you want to meet Bowen?” And I was like, “Oh my God, yes.” So then she [says], “Oh, hey, this is Hoku. This is Bowen.” And then his face was just blank. And I was like, “Oh my God, okay, this is going to be so awkward.” And then he goes, “Sorry, what was your name?” And I’m like, “Hoku.”
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_101-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_102-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> Then his face lit up. He’s like, “Hoku. Oh my God, you’re Hoku.” He goes, “You’re the person I was most excited to see.” And I was like, “You’re the person I was most excited to see.” Anyway, we’re friends now. He’s basically my bestie. Then Matt was so sweet. That was a really cool moment.
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_103-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_104-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> It was [also] fun to talk to <a class="null" href="https://people.com/tag/reese-witherspoon/" data-component="link" data-source="inlineLink" data-type="internalLink" data-ordinal="1" rel="null">Reese [Witherspoon]</a> again because we’d spent a day in London together shooting this music video. She was just so excited that I was there and clearly such a fan of the song and so proud that it was connected to <em>Elle</em> and everything. There’s a video of her while I was performing, singing along on “Perfect Day.” She’s really championed it. Over the years, she’s done videos with “Perfect Day” in it. I’m just really grateful that she’s embraced my connection to it as well. 
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_105-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>

<p id="mntl-sc-block_107-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> <strong>PEOPLE: This year Bowen and Matt </strong><a class="null" href="https://people.com/matt-rogers-recalls-how-mandy-moore-reacted-when-asked-to-sing-at-culturistas-awards-12008476" data-component="link" data-source="inlineLink" data-type="internalLink" data-ordinal="1" rel="null"><strong>performed “Only Hope” with Mandy Moore</strong></a><strong> at the Las Culturistas Awards, which is incredible. What if they did something similar for “Perfect Day” with you? </strong>
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_108-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_109-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> <strong>HOKU: </strong>Oh my God, that would be amazing. Let’s just both put that out in the universe.
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_110-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_111-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> <strong>PEOPLE: I’ve heard you’re back in the recording studio. Can you tell me what you’ve been working on?</strong>
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_112-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_113-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> <strong>HOKU: </strong>I’m putting together an album based on a bunch of songs that I think would really be good for [it]. There’s stuff that I would like to have out in the world. Any interaction I have on social media, it’s like, “When’s the comeback? When’s the new music?” And there were a lot of years where I wasn’t really writing songs that would feel like they fit into the Hoku universe. Writing is how I process things and get things out of my body, and so, for a long time there were songs that were me just trying to process who I was after being a pop star was over, and then who I was as a mom. And for a long time, it was who I was in my faith before I stepped away from that.
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_114-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_115-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> The timing is really perfect because over the last many years I’ve been in this really joyful, open-hearted state. My kids are in their teens and pre-teens. We’ve had a lot of fun. They’re great kids, and there’s a little bit of that sense of being able to step back and just enjoy your handiwork. I was already gearing up [for new music] before I was reached out to for the “Elle World” event. I was like, “Oh my God, this is perfect timing.” Because I was already getting ready to, in my own way, think of how I was going to relaunch, and this just gave me a huge springboard. 
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_116-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>

<p id="mntl-sc-block_119-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> <strong>PEOPLE: Are you signed to a label at this point?</strong>
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_120-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_121-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> <strong>HOKU: </strong>No, I’m not signed to a label at this point. I was kind of trying to see how much I could do on my own. My label experience wasn’t great. I know things are much different now, but I haven’t really pursued that yet. I’d imagine at a certain point that might be necessary, but there’s a lot that you can do now without a label. It’s something I’m open to but haven’t begun to pursue.
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_122-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_123-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> <strong>PEOPLE: Have you been asked — or would you — create a song for </strong><a class="null" href="https://people.com/elle-cast-side-by-side-legally-blonde-actors-characters-12008473" data-component="link" data-source="inlineLink" data-type="internalLink" data-ordinal="1" rel="null"><strong>the TV show </strong></a><a class="null" href="https://people.com/elle-cast-side-by-side-legally-blonde-actors-characters-12008473" data-component="link" data-source="inlineLink" data-type="internalLink" data-ordinal="2" rel="null"><strong><em>Elle</em></strong></a><strong>?</strong>
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_124-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_125-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> <strong>HOKU: </strong>I’d be open to any and everything like that. I think I hid for a lot of years and just enjoyed my anonymity, enjoyed the peace I was able to give my kids, but we’re all good now. Now I feel more freed up energetically to put all of that towards getting back into spreading joy to the world through my music and bringing some of that joy and nostalgia back. I’m doing songwriting stuff behind the scenes. I’ve been doing that a little bit over the years and stuff, so that’s already something I’m definitely in. It would just be fun. 
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_126-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_127-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> <strong>PEOPLE: Do you have plans to tour in the future?</strong>
</p>
<div id="mntl-sc-block_128-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-adslot mntl-block"></div>
<p id="mntl-sc-block_129-0" class="comp mntl-sc-block mntl-sc-block-html"> <strong>HOKU:</strong> I would love to tour. I’d be super down to do that. Bring it on.
</p></div></div>
